name: CodeSnippet
description: Syntax-highlighted code block with a language picker, optional line numbers, and a copy button.

a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-05-28 — Promoted from alpha: Example + ForcedColors stories present; Storybook axe gate enabled. 2026-07-08 — captured Default and Example accessibility-tree snapshots plus a real Playwright forced-colors snapshot; stable remains blocked until the Figma URL points at a real numeric node id. 2026-07-10 — Figma component set built (Molecules, node 1161-2809: Inline/Single/Multi variants, DT token bindings); promoted to stable with RhythmguardPage as production consumer.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the snippet region.

allowCopy.description: Show the copy button; keep on for reusable code.

variant.description: Layout variant: inline token, single line, or multi-line window.

maxLines.description: Clamp height to this many lines; longer code scrolls. 0 disables the clamp.

onCopy.description: Fires after the code is copied to the clipboard.

forbiddenUse: Bypass design tokens or skip forced-colors verification at beta.
dense: Prism-highlighted code block: language set (ts/js/html/python/go/rust/json/bash/...), showLineNumbers, allowCopy button w/ onCopy hook, maxLines clamp, variant surface; aria-label for AT context

usage.description: CodeSnippet renders highlighted code from a `code` string: pick `language` from the supported set, toggle `showLineNumbers`, and keep `allowCopy` on for anything a reader might reuse (wire `onCopy` for analytics). `maxLines` clamps tall blocks behind a scroll. Give non-obvious blocks an `aria-label` naming what the code is. For a titled, framed presentation with captions, compose it inside CodeBlockWindow.

bestPractices.description: Set language explicitly; unhighlighted code reads as a rendering bug in docs.
Keep allowCopy on for reusable code; the copy affordance is the whole point of a snippet.
Use maxLines on long listings so surrounding prose stays reachable.
Give the block an aria-label describing what the code is ("Install command").
Do not use it for one-word inline code in prose — that is an inline code element, not a block snippet.
Do not paste secrets or live tokens into examples; snippets get copied verbatim.
